# Perturbation Recipes

Each recipe below is one or more entries for the `conditions:` list in
`config/ChromSimConfig.yaml`, with what it models, what to expect, and what to
watch out for. Every recipe works with the current pipeline: nothing to install
or code. The numbers are examples of the pattern, not recommendations: run a
small range and see which value matches your data.

All recipes follow the rules from the [vignette](vignette.qmd#adding-a-condition-to-test-a-hypothesis):
change **one** setting relative to a condition you already have, give each
entry a new `name` and `params_name`, and count the cost: every condition adds
`n_replicates × n_shards` GPU jobs per locus (6 with the shipped settings).

## How the settings relate

The cohesin settings are not independent. Three relations explain most of
what the recipes do:

| Quantity | Formula | Shipped value |
|----------|---------|---------------|
| DNA extruded per cohesin leg before it falls off (processivity) | `lifetime × vlef` monomers | 75,000 × 0.0025 ≈ 190 kb |
| Number of cohesins on the chain | chain monomers / `separation` | one per 240 kb |
| Loop coverage: how much of the chain is inside a loop at once | about 2 × processivity / `separation` | ≈ 1.6 |

So doubling `lifetime` doubles how far each cohesin gets; halving `vlef` with
the same `lifetime` halves it; doubling `separation` halves the number of
cohesins. One monomer is `resolution` bp (1 kb by default).

All recipes below start from this baseline (the shipped `cond1_baseline`):

```yaml
  - name:         cond1_baseline
    params_name:  baseline
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1
```

## Cohesin stays longer (WAPL loss)

**Models:** loss of WAPL, which releases cohesin from DNA, so cohesin stays
bound and extrudes further.

```yaml
  - name:         wapl-loss_2x
    params_name:  wapl_2x
    lifetime:     150000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1

  - name:         wapl-loss_5x
    params_name:  wapl_5x
    lifetime:     375000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1
```

**Expect:** longer loops, reaching convergent CTCF pairs further apart, and
stronger stripes, as reported in WAPL-depleted Hi-C.

**Watch out:** a longer `lifetime` also needs longer equilibration; polysim
extends its warm-up to at least one cohesin lifetime automatically, so these
jobs take longer.

## Fewer cohesins (NIPBL or RAD21 depletion)

**Models:** partial loss of cohesin loading (NIPBL) or of cohesin itself
(RAD21 knockdown). Halving the amount of cohesin doubles `separation`.

```yaml
  - name:         cohesin-50pct
    params_name:  cohesin_50
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   480
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1
```

**Expect:** weaker loops and domains everywhere, with the same positions.

**Watch out:** complete cohesin loss (`separation` with no cohesin at all)
isn't expressible yet; very large values (e.g. 5000) approach it.

## Weaker CTCF stalling (partial CTCF depletion)

**Models:** less CTCF bound at every site (a partial knockdown, or a mutant
that holds cohesin less well), without data on which sites are lost.

```yaml
  - name:         ctcf-weak_0.25
    params_name:  ctcf_025
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.25
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1
```

**Expect:** weaker dots and boundaries, and more cohesin reading through
sites to the next convergent pair.

**Watch out:** this weakens every site equally. If you have CTCF data from the
perturbed cells, the next recipe is more faithful.

## CTCF degradation, with data

**Models:** a CTCF degron (auxin or dTAG) or any treatment where you profiled
CTCF. The sites themselves come from the perturbed sample.

Add the perturbed sample to the samplesheet (its Hi-C is optional):

```
Project  Cell_Type  Condition    CTCF_Peaks                              Hi-C
MyProj   mESC       untreated    /proj/yourlab/ctcf/untreated.narrowPeak    /proj/yourlab/hic/untreated.mcool
MyProj   mESC       ctcf_degron  /proj/yourlab/ctcf/auxin_6h.narrowPeak     /proj/yourlab/hic/auxin_6h.mcool
```

Then one condition per sample, identical except for the CTCF they use:

```yaml
  - name:         untreated
    params_name:  untreated
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    untreated
    compare_hic:  untreated

  - name:         ctcf-degron
    params_name:  degron
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    ctcf_degron
    compare_hic:  ctcf_degron
```

**Expect:** loops lost where the degron removes CTCF from an anchor; this is
the same design as the sorbitol `cond2_ctcf-only` condition.

**Watch out:** names, paths and assemblies must agree; run
`bash check_inputs.sh` after adding the samples.

## Stalled cohesin lives longer (or not)

**Models:** how much CTCF stabilizes cohesin once both legs are stalled
(`life_boost_stalled`, default 4 from the `polysim:` block). `1` means no
stabilization.

```yaml
  - name:         no-stall-boost
    params_name:  boost_1
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    life_boost_stalled: 1
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1
```

**Expect:** with `1`, weaker dots at convergent pairs, since loops there come
apart as fast as anywhere else; with larger values, stronger dots.

## Slower extrusion

**Models:** cohesin stepping more slowly, e.g. under reduced ATP, or a
mutant motor.

```yaml
  - name:         slow-extrusion
    params_name:  slow
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    vlef:         0.00125
    ctcf_type:    condition1
    compare_hic:  condition1
```

**Expect:** with the same `lifetime`, half the processivity (≈ 95 kb per
leg), so shorter loops and fewer distant dots.

**Watch out:** `vlef` and `lifetime` trade off (processivity is their
product). To change speed but not loop size, change both: `vlef: 0.00125`
with `lifetime: 150000`.

## A robustness range

Before trusting a conclusion, check it holds over a few cohesin settings,
for every condition you compare. For example, three lifetimes for the
control–treated pair from the sorbitol example (6 conditions):

```yaml
  - {name: ctl_life-0.5x, params_name: ctl_l05, lifetime: 37500,  separation: 240, ctcf_capture: 0.5, ctcf_type: condition1, compare_hic: condition1}
  - {name: ctl_life-1x,   params_name: ctl_l1,  lifetime: 75000,  separation: 240, ctcf_capture: 0.5, ctcf_type: condition1, compare_hic: condition1}
  - {name: ctl_life-2x,   params_name: ctl_l2,  lifetime: 150000, separation: 240, ctcf_capture: 0.5, ctcf_type: condition1, compare_hic: condition1}
  - {name: trt_life-0.5x, params_name: trt_l05, lifetime: 37500,  separation: 240, ctcf_capture: 0.5, ctcf_type: condition2, compare_hic: condition2}
  - {name: trt_life-1x,   params_name: trt_l1,  lifetime: 75000,  separation: 240, ctcf_capture: 0.5, ctcf_type: condition2, compare_hic: condition2}
  - {name: trt_life-2x,   params_name: trt_l2,  lifetime: 150000, separation: 240, ctcf_capture: 0.5, ctcf_type: condition2, compare_hic: condition2}
```

This is YAML's one-line form of the same entries: each `{...}` is one
condition. If the control-vs-treated conclusion (e.g. "CTCF explains the lost
loops") holds at all three lifetimes, it doesn't depend on that choice.

## Simulating without Hi-C

A sample with CTCF peaks but no Hi-C (`NA` in the samplesheet) can still be
simulated: leave `compare_hic` out of its condition. You get the simulated
maps, P(s), insulation and APA, without the comparison metrics. This is how to
make a prediction for a condition you haven't measured yet.

```yaml
  - name:         prediction_noHiC
    params_name:  pred
    lifetime:     75000
    separation:   240
    ctcf_capture: 0.5
    ctcf_type:    my_ctcf_only_sample
```
